title: Formal approximation along the punctured power-series zero section
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative local ring of depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $d>0$, set $B=A[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and let $z:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be induced by constant coefficient [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $V\subset Y$ be open with $z^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m_A\}$. Write $U=z^{-1}(V)$ and $z_V:U\to V$ for the restriction of $z$. For $x\in U$, write $g_x:\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to\mathcal O_{V,z_V(x)}$ for the germ map. Let $r:B\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ be canonical restriction and $J_x=\ker(\mathcal O_{V,z_V(x)}\to\mathcal O_{U,x})$. For every $s\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ there is a unique $b\in B$ such that $g_x(s-r(b))\in J_x^n$ for every $x\in U$ and $n\ge0$.

proof.text: Apply depth-two Hartogs to the structure module of Spec A, obtaining Gamma(U,O_U)=A. The only missing point is the maximal ideal, whose local ring and structure-module stalk are A.

Let I=(X_1,...,X_d). Modulo I^n, a power series is uniquely the finite sum of its monomials of total degree less than n: the coefficient functions on these monomials and the corresponding monomial vectors give mutually inverse A-linear maps. Push the n-th thickening forward to U via its finite affine map. Its module is the finite direct sum of these copies of O_U, so Hartogs computes its sections as B/I^n. Restrictions between thickenings discard the higher degree coefficients, hence are the usual quotient maps.

The reductions of s on the thickenings give a compatible family in B/I^n. Completeness and separatedness for the ideal of variables give a unique b in B with those reductions. Explicitly its coefficient at a monomial of degree e is the coefficient of that monomial in the reduction modulo I^(e+1); compatibility proves independence and uniqueness.

Use the canonical localization description of the stalk map of Spec(constantCoeff), and the stalk isomorphisms for the open restrictions. In these coordinates it is B_q to A_p, r/t mapping to cc(r)/cc(t), where q=cc^{-1}(p). Its kernel is I B_q: a numerator mapping to zero after localization is killed modulo I by a denominator outside p. The n-th thickening stalk is (B/I^n)_q=B_q/(I B_q)^n, since localization sends I^n to (I B_q)^n. Hence its two section germs agree precisely when their difference is in J_x^n. Equality at every stalk of the thickening is equality of its sections, which translates both existence and uniqueness from the preceding step to the stated predicate.

theorem existsUnique_powerSeries_punctured_formal_approximation
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := A) A)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d)
    (V : (Spec (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A))).Opens)
    (hV : ∀ x : Spec (.of A),
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (σ := Fin d)))) x ∈ V ↔
        x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) :
    let z := Spec.map
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (σ := Fin d) (R := A)))
    let r := ((ΓSpecIso (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A))).inv ≫ V.ι.appTop).hom
    ∀ s : Γ(V.toScheme, ⊤), ∃! b : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) A,
      ∀ (x : (z ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme) (n : ℕ),
        (V.toScheme.presheaf.Γgerm ((z ∣_ V) x)).hom (s - r b) ∈
          (RingHom.ker ((z ∣_ V).stalkMap x).hom) ^ n
